subject: Renewal roadmap: flex burst (on-demand) & co-term sequencing
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta@brightwell.ai>

Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal window + potential burst credits / co-term

Hi Grace,

Hope you're well — our renewal for BrightWell's Dedicated pool comes up in mid-August and we've been reviewing next-year capacity. Usage spiked in Q2 as we piloted a new feature, and we expect intermittent burst events for a launch in September (short windows, high TPS).

Two asks up front:
- Can Redwood offer an on-demand "burst" credit bucket we can tap into for short peaks without committing to an uplifted monthly baseline?
- We would like to align the renewal with another product team's contract (co-term) — how flexible is Redwood on mid-contract alignment/proration and staged credits?

Attached is a high-level usage snapshot for Q2 so you can see spike shape. We also want any pricing change to protect us from a big step-up if peaks are short-lived.

Could we get a quick sketch of options and a 30-minute sync next week?

Thanks,
Marta Lopez
Director, Cloud Infrastructure
BrightWell Health

Subject: Re: Renewal window + potential burst credits / co-term

Marta — thanks for the snapshot and the heads up. High level response before we sync:

- Yes, we can design a hybrid path: a modest committed uplift (protects unit pricing) + an on-demand burst bucket you draw against at a higher per-token premium. Burst credits would be short-lived, billed only when consumed, and expire at quarter-end unless rolled for a small fee.
- Co-terming mid-contract is doable; typical approach is pro-rata true-up for the shorter contract and a voucher-style credit applied to the longer term. We'll show two co-term flows (staged voucher vs. annualize uplift) with dollar math.

I've looped in Ben (pricing/AM) to prepare two concrete options and Irene (CS ops) for capacity/ops notes. Can you do a 30-min call on Tue 14th at 11am PT or Wed 15th at 9am PT?

I'll send a one-page options deck before the call.

Best,

Subject: Re: Renewal window + potential burst credits / co-term

Marta — thanks for pulling the usage. Attached is a first-pass term sheet (BrightWell_renewal_options_v1.pdf) with three practical paths:

1) Safety-First Hybrid (recommended for bursty launches)
   - +20% committed uplift on baseline for 12 months (keeps base unit price)
   - On-demand Burst Bucket: prepaid credits you purchase at a 50% premium and draw down as needed; unused credits expire quarterly
   - Co-term: voucher applied to remaining months of the shorter contract, balances pro-rated

2) Elastic Commit
   - Minimal committed uplift (+5%) with automated short-term upgrades when sustained usage > 2x baseline for 48hrs
   - No prepaid credits; auto-billing at a higher per-token rate for transient spikes

3) Annualize with Ramp Discount
   - Annualized higher commit (protects capacity) with graduated discount tiers; suitable if you retain sustained higher throughput after launch

Notes: we included dollarized examples using your Q2 snapshot (see appendix). For procurement/finance — DocuSign link is in the deck for the draft amendment; legal redlines are usually limited to SLA windows and indemnity language.

Call confirmed: Tue 14th at 11am PT (I'll be on). I'll bring final numbers and the DocuSign preview.

Attachments: BrightWell_renewal_options_v1.pdf

- For Option 1, can unused prepaid burst credits be partially carried (e.g., 25%) into next quarter rather than full expiry? That would help us manage missed forecasts.
- For Option 2, what is the auto-billing cap to prevent runaway spend (can we set a monthly hard cap that requires manual approval to exceed)?

Also, small ask for procurement: can you provide a single landscape table that shows the net effective $/token across the three options at low/median/high scenarios? That will help our finance team with quick comparatives.

Marta — great questions. Follow-up notes and actions from today's sync: 

- Unused burst credits: we'll allow 25% carryover to the following quarter for Option 1; remaining credits expire. We'll add a small administrative fee (1.5% of carried value).
- Auto-billing cap for Option 2: we can set a configurable hard cap per month with automatic notification and a manual approval flow to exceed the cap. Finance can own the approval step.
- SLA / deprioritization: Redwood's policy is to avoid deprioritization for paid Dedicated tiers. For burst credits (on-demand), in the rare case of regional capacity constraints we will surface a one-hour notice and offer immediate routing to an alternate region or temporary rate increase — never silent throttling. Legal suggested a short carveout in the amendment; Irene will attach the ops note.

Deliverables we committed to: 
1) Finalized one-page comparative table (net $/token at low/median/high scenarios) — Ben will send by EOD Wed 21st.
2) Amended term sheet with the 25% carryover and cap mechanics — Ben to circulate for initial redlines.
3) Ops confirmation (Irene): latency expectations when burst routing is active + runbook link.
